cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: ____ is the value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made.
cards.answer: Opportunity cost exists because resources are scarce: choosing one thing always means giving up another.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: Why does a production possibility curve usually bow outwards from the origin?
cards.answer: Resources are not equally good at making both goods. Moving more into one good uses less suitable resources, so the opportunity cost keeps rising.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: The reward for the factor of production enterprise is ____.
cards.answer: Profit. Land earns rent, labour earns wages and capital earns interest.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: A ____ good is non-rival and non-excludable, so the free market will not provide it.
cards.answer: Public good, e.g. street lighting. Non-excludable people cannot be stopped from using it, which creates the free rider problem.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: A change in the good's own price causes a ____ demand curve.
cards.answer: Movement along the curve. A change in any other factor, like income or the price of a substitute, shifts the whole curve.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: Price rises, quantity demanded falls. Find the line with the mistake.
lines: PED = % change in price ÷ % change in quantity
cards.answer: Line 3 is upside down. PED = % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price = -10 ÷ 20 = -0.5, so demand is price inelastic.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: A good has a negative income elasticity of demand. What kind of good is it?
cards.answer: An inferior good: when incomes rise, people buy less of it and switch to better alternatives, e.g. bus travel or cheap own-brand food.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: Two goods with a positive cross elasticity of demand are ____.
cards.answer: Substitutes: if the price of Coke rises, demand for Pepsi rises. Complements, like printers and ink, have a negative XED.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: Studies estimate the price elasticity of demand for cigarettes. Roughly what value?
cards.answer: About -0.4: demand is price inelastic because smoking is addictive and has few substitutes. That is why cigarette taxes raise a lot of revenue.

cards.subject: economics
cards.hook: You would pay $50 for a concert ticket, but it costs $30. What is the $20 called?
cards.answer: Consumer surplus: what you are willing to pay minus what you actually pay. On a diagram it is the area under the demand curve and above the price.
